summary: The sample implements the core async Beanie+FastAPI pipeline, sends uploaded documents to OpenAI, validates with Pydantic, models customers with Beanie, and upserts on a government_id key. Secrets are read from the environment and a .env.example is provided. Key gaps: (1) connection timeout/retry parameters recommended by the documentdb-connection guidance were not applied, (2) index creation via the MCP tooling failed because management/write tools are opt-in in this environment, (3) the seed script is not idempotent in all cases and index-creation/verification was not completed programmatically, and (4) a few gallery checklist items (search endpoints, unit tests, infra-as-code) are missing. The build choices are mostly reasonable and recorded; one builder choice (Beanie vs Beanie2 / Motor vs AsyncMongoClient) was made in code but the decision log attempt failed and is missing a final recorded decision. See requirement-by-requirement results, practice checks, decision reviews and documentation gaps below.

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline accepts uploaded KYC documents as its input (e.g. a file upload or document bytes handed to an ingestion entry point).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/main.py lines 16-23 (FastAPI /upload handler reading UploadFile and file.read()).

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline is written in async Python, with the OpenAI calls and the Beanie ODM database operations awaited.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/openai_client.py defines async extract_entities and app/src/app/main.py awaits extract_entities (line 26) and awaits cust.upsert() (line 40).

requirement_results.requirement: Each uploaded document is sent to OpenAI with a request for structured entity extraction covering name, DOB, address and ID numbers.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/openai_client.py PROMPT_TEMPLATE (lines 12-22) requests name, dob, address, government_id and main.py calls extract_entities (line 26).

requirement_results.requirement: A Pydantic schema declares the extracted entities (name, DOB, address, ID numbers), and the OpenAI output is validated against that schema before it is stored.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/schemas.py defines ExtractionSchema and main.py constructs ExtractionSchema(**extracted) on line 29 before mapping to Customer.

requirement_results.requirement: The customer record is modelled as a Beanie ODM Document, and a validated record is upserted into Azure DocumentDB through Beanie (updated when a matching customer already exists, inserted otherwise; matched on e.g. an ID number).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/models.py defines class Customer(Document) with an upsert() method that calls replace_one({'government_id': self.government_id}, self, upsert=True) (lines 13-21, 33-39). main.py constructs Customer and calls await cust.upsert() (main.py lines 31-41).

requirement_results.requirement: A record whose extraction fails schema validation or lacks required entities is stored as incomplete and flagged for manual review (e.g. a review flag on the stored document).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/models.py: Customer.status defaults to 'manual_review' (line 19) set_complete_if_valid toggles status to 'complete' only if all fields present (lines 26-31). For missing government_id, upsert inserts (lines 33-38) leaving status 'manual_review'.

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment (lines 8-12). app/src/app/openai_client.py reads OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL from environment (lines 7-10). app/.env.example contains placeholders (app/.env.example lines 2-4). No real secrets are committed.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: .env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL (app/.env.example lines 1-4). README instructs to copy .env.example (app/README.md lines 21-25).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add any runtime variables the app relies on (for example DATABASE_NAME or MONGODB_DATABASE / DB_NAME if you want explicit database selection) to .env.example and document their use in README; e.g., add DB_NAME=sample_fintech_05.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: This sample does not compute or store embeddings and has no vector-index creation code.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If you add embeddings, document the embedding model and set vector index dims to the model's output size in the index-creation script or README.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector index or embedding code present.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Only applicable if embeddings are added; provide index-creation helper with parameters and README guidance.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app/db.py defines a module-level _client and init_db() sets _client = AsyncIOMotorClient(uri) (lines 6, 14-21); startup event calls init_db() (app/src/app/main.py lines 12-15).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: scripts/seed.py exists and uploads three sample documents to the /upload endpoint (scripts/seed.py lines 8-12, 14-22). The app declares a unique index via Beanie's model (models.py line 17) but MCP index creation failed in this run (events.jsonl documentdb_create_index exception). The seed script uses POST to /upload (which upserts on government_id only when provided), but two of the three seed samples have no government_id so repeated runs would produce duplicates.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make the seed script idempotent by providing government_id for all seed samples or change the seed to call an upsert endpoint directly with deterministic keys; also add a script to create/verify indexes idempotently (createIndex with if-not-exists pattern or use Beanie init to create indexes on startup and document how to run it).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: There is no /search endpoint in app/src/app/main.py.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a /search endpoint that validates input, returns 400 for empty queries, wraps embedding/LLM calls with try/except, and returns clear error messages when embedding fails.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If you add semantic search, include similarity scores in the HTTP response and document the score semantics in README.

requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins fastapi==0.95.2, uvicorn[standard]==0.22.0, beanie==1.16.4, motor==3.5.3, pydantic==1.10.12, openai==1.0.0, pytest==7.4.2, httpx==0.24.1 (app/requirements.txt).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: No test files present in the repository; pytest is listed in requirements but no unit tests or mocking harness provided.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests with mocked OpenAI and mocked database clients (e.g., using pytest + pytest-asyncio + respx/httpx mocking or monkeypatching Beanie/Motor) so tests run offline.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No Bicep/Terraform/ARM templates or infra-as-code files found in the repository.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal Bicep/ARM/Terraform snippet (Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters) or a link to the documentdb-azure-deployment skill example, if you want to provide infra as code.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md contains Overview, Prerequisites, Setup, Run instructions and Cleanup (app/README.md lines 3-39, 41-45).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and code name the target service 'Azure DocumentDB' (app/README.md lines 5, 10).

checks.practice: When using drivers, prefer a single shared MongoClient instance per process (connection-pool singleton) instead of creating a client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/app/db.py lines 6, 14-21: module-level _client is assigned AsyncIOMotorClient(uri) in init_db() and reused.

checks.practice: Require TLS for all client connections to Azure DocumentDB (connection strings include tls=true) and use certificate validation in production; configure sensible driver timeouts so code fails fast.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example includes tls=true (app/.env.example line 2) and db.py comments note TLS is required (app/src/app/db.py line 17) but no driver timeout parameters (serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS) are set on AsyncIOMotorClient (app/src/app/db.py line 19).
checks.fix: Set sensible timeouts when creating the client, e.g. AsyncIOMotorClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, socketTimeoutMS=60000) or parse and append serverSelectionTimeoutMS to the URI.

checks.practice: Driver version is pinned and is one the service supports.
checks.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins beanie==1.16.4 and motor==3.5.3 (app/requirements.txt). Quickstarts list tested combinations (Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient) but the sample pins Motor+Beanie 1; the code runs with the pinned packages.
checks.source: Quickstart: Connect Beanie to Azure DocumentDB
checks.searched: learn.microsoft.com quickstart Beanie tested driver versions
checks.fix: Consider aligning pinned versions with the published quickstart (Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient) or add a README note explaining the chosen Beanie/Motor versions and any incompatibilities.

checks.practice: Create a unique index for the stable upsert key used by the pipeline (for example government_id) to prevent duplicates and make upserts deterministic.
checks.evidence: app/src/app/models.py declares government_id: Optional[Indexed(str, unique=True)] (line 17). The upsert method uses replace_one with upsert=True (lines 33-39).

checks.practice: Avoid storing large binary files or multi-megabyte payloads in DocumentDB documents; keep only metadata and structured fields in the database and store raw files in blob storage or other object storage.
checks.evidence: The app accepts file uploads but decodes text and stores structured fields and raw extraction; it does not persist the uploaded binary file into the DB (main.py lines 16-23, 31-37). README warns that only text uploads are supported and suggests adding OCR and storing raw files in blob storage (app/README.md lines 31-35).

checks.practice: Handle transient faults with bounded retries that use exponential backoff (and jitter) and only retry operations that are safe to replay.
checks.evidence: No retry/backoff logic around the OpenAI call or DB operations. openai_client.extract_entities will raise and be translated to HTTP 500 (openai_client.py lines 24-39 and main.py lines 25-28). DB upsert operations are executed without explicit retry/backoff (models.py upsert uses replace_one directly).
checks.fix: Wrap non-idempotent operations in retries with exponential backoff and jitter where safe, or rely on driver retry settings for idempotent operations; for OpenAI calls use bounded retries and circuit-breakers for transient network errors.

checks.practice: When public guidance is absent for framework-specific initialization (e.g., Beanie-specific init rules), follow framework docs and treat service-level guidance as application policy.
checks.evidence: The app uses init_beanie(database=_client.get_default_database(), document_models=[Customer]) in db.py line 21; this matches common Beanie init usage, but there is known public guidance recommending Beanie 2 + AsyncMongoClient in some quickstarts.

checks.what_would_help: A short authoritative note in product docs about recommended async client patterns for Beanie (Motor vs AsyncMongoClient) would remove ambiguity.

checks.practice: When using OpenAI or other LLMs in a pipeline, validate outputs server-side and persist only validated structured fields while preserving raw responses in a non-indexed raw field for auditing.
checks.evidence: openai_client.extract_entities parses JSON and returns a 'raw' fallback when parsing fails (openai_client.py lines 41-50). decision_reviews.comment: Approving the build as 'ready_with_gaps' is a reasonable operator-level decision. The log entry exists (decisions.jsonl) and fits the recorded readiness state.
Choosing Python 3.13 is supported by the readiness report and build logs (pip installs ran). events.jsonl includes the readiness evidence quoted.
Reading secrets from environment matches the prompt instruction and the code: db.py and openai_client.py read environment variables. Evidence: prompt and code lines referenced.

Choosing gpt-4o-mini is a sensible default for an extraction sample. However the decision's reason_source is 'model_default' (decisions.jsonl) rather than a documented product recommendation; per the audit rules this should be documented explicitly in sample README or product guidance so other builders don't pick different models unexpectedly.

Upserting by government_id and creating a unique index is implemented in code (models.py uses Indexed(..., unique=True) and upsert uses replace_one with upsert=True). The decision matches implementation.
Using the existing cluster and not provisioning new resources follows the run policy and readiness report. The decision is consistent with build actions.
Selecting motor==3.5.3 because a later motor release was unavailable on PyPI in this environment is supported by the pip install traces in events.jsonl; the change is recorded in requirements.txt.
Selecting openai==1.0.0 based on available PyPI versions is supported by the pip traces. Implementation uses the older ChatCompletion.create surface invoked in a thread, matching the selected client.

Choosing to create/verify the unique index via the documentdb MCP server was reasonable. However the attempt to create the index and insert a seed document failed because management/write MCP tools are disabled by default in this environment (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException for documentdb_create_index and documentdb_insert_documents). The plan was sound but the verification step did not succeed; the decision should have included an environment check or fallback plan (e.g., create indexes on app init) and the run should log the failed MCP calls (which it does).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The .env.example omits an explicit DB_NAME / MONGODB_DATABASE variable and does not document MCP opt-in flags (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS / ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS) that the build environment required to run management operations.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository (.env.example, README) and Microsoft Learn quickstarts for Beanie and MongoDB connection patterns.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Small: the sample runs but verification steps relying on environment flags and an explicit DB name were not automated; index creation via MCP failed in this run and the README leaves DB selection implicit.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Update .env.example with DB_NAME=MONGODB_DATABASE=sample_fintech_05 and document optional flags for MCP verification (e.g., 'To allow automated MCP index creation during CI/local verification set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true and ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS=true in your verification environment; this is opt-in by design'). Add a short README subsection 'Runtime variables' listing each env var, default, and example.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The seed script uploads sample documents but is not fully idempotent (two sample documents lack government_id so re-running the seed creates duplicates). There is no programmatic, idempotent index creation script that works in the default verification environment without enabling MCP write/management flags.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository scripts/seed.py and events.jsonl (MCP create_index tool call failed).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Medium: prevented automated verification of index creation and made seed runs non-idempotent in some cases; the builder had to leave index creation as a manual step in README.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a seed-and-init script that: (1) uses deterministic government_id values for all seed records (so upserts are idempotent), (2) creates declared indexes via Beanie init_beanie (documented) or via the MCP API but only after a runtime opt-in check, and (3) can be re-run safely without duplicating data. Document how to run the script and the expected result (e.g., 'After running init_seed.py twice the collection still contains three customers').

doc_gaps.topic: Connection timeout & retry guidance for async clients
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The product skill and quickstarts describe TLS and provide examples for timeouts, but the sample did not add explicit driver timeout/query settings or example code showing safe defaults (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS).
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection skill, quickstart docs (learn.microsoft.com references), repo code (app/src/app/db.py).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Low/Medium: lack of driver timeouts can cause long-hanging requests in poor-network conditions; the sample leaves this to readers rather than demonstrating recommended settings.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short rule or code snippet to the documentdb-connection skill and sample README showing how to instantiate an AsyncIOMotorClient with safe defaults, for example: AsyncIOMotorClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, socketTimeoutMS=60000, maxPoolSize=50). Explain the trade-offs and point to the skill for tuning guidance.

doc_gaps.topic: Beanie + async client authoritative guidance (Motor vs AsyncMongoClient)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Public guidance about exact recommended async client patterns for Beanie (Motor vs PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient) and the tested Beanie + driver combinations is scattered; prior-knowledge choices led to differing sample implementations.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn Beanie quickstarts, documentdb-driver and documentdb-connection skill resources, and general searches for 'Azure DocumentDB Beanie Motor'.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Medium: the builder chose Motor + Beanie (Beanie 1.x pattern) and pinned motor==3.5.3; quickstarts show Beanie 2 with AsyncMongoClient as a tested combination. This ambiguity may lead readers to mismatch versions or run into subtle incompatibilities.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A one-page 'Beanie + Azure DocumentDB' note in product docs or the documentdb-connection skill that: (a) lists recommended Beanie versions and the corresponding async client (Motor vs AsyncMongoClient), (b) shows a minimal init example for each supported pattern, and (c) lists known tested combinations (Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient with specific tested versions).

doc_gaps.topic: Recommended OpenAI model & embedding dimension mapping
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The build made a model choice (gpt-4o-mini) via a model_default decision; product documentation does not state a recommended extraction/embedding model or embedding dimensionality to use in samples.
doc_gaps.where_searched: decisions.jsonl (D004), openai_client.py (OPENAI_MODEL default), and discovered practice searches for embedding dims.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Low: the sample defaults to gpt-4o-mini; if a future sample adds embeddings, not pinning the embedding model and dims may cause mismatch with vector-index parameters.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add guidance in the sample README or a product 'LLM integrations' page recommending a default text-extraction model for structured extraction and the embedding model (with explicit output dimensions) to use for vector indexes. If you do not want to mandate a model, document that the embedding dimension must be set to the model's output vector size and show examples for common choices (e.g., OpenAI 'text-embedding-3-small' -> 1536 dims).

doc_gaps.topic: MCP tool opt-in discoverability and verification fallback
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The build's programmatic attempts to create indexes and insert seed docs via MCP failed because management and write tools are disabled by default and require opt-in flags (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException with guidance to set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS/ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS).
doc_gaps.where_searched: events.jsonl MCP tool failure logs and the MCP skill docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: High for automated verification: it prevented automated index creation and seed insertion during this run, which forced the builder to leave index creation as a manual step.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Document the MCP opt-in requirements prominently in the MCP skill and in the sample README, including the exact env vars (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS, ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS) and recommended security considerations for enabling them in CI or local debugging. Provide a fallback approach for verification that uses the app's init_db() to create indexes if MCP calls fail.

doc_gaps.topic: Unit testing without a live cluster
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No unit tests or mocking harness were included to allow offline verification of parsing, schema validation, and logic.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository (no tests folder) and requirements.txt showing pytest present.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Medium: maintainers and reviewers cannot run behavior-preserving tests offline; missing tests reduce confidence in behavior changes.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a tests/ directory with pytest-based unit tests that mock openai.Client responses and mock or stub Beanie/Motor operations (or use a simple in-memory replacement). Include instructions in README how to run tests locally without a live cluster.
